models_evaluated: five open-weight LLMs (names not given in text)

links.outcome: Sycophancy rate with versus without grounding in retrieved or curated context
links.effect: Grounding reduced sycophancy but did not eliminate it (no numbers in abstract).
links.quote: Grounding helps, but does not eliminate the behavior.

links.outcome: Model susceptibility to user pushback and framing variations (role, evidence, structure)
links.effect: Sycophancy nearly three times more common when users challenge an answer already given than when the false claim is in the initial query; higher for users presented as physicians or medical students.
links.quote: Medical sycophancy is nearly three times more common when users challenge an answer the model has already given than when the false claim appears in the initial query.

unlisted_practices: Selecting benchmark questions carefully because sycophancy varies more across questions than across models

screen.reason: Evaluates medical sycophancy across LLMs under conversational challenge factors, specifically testing retrieval grounding as an intervention/safeguard to mitigate sycophancy.
